name: FileDeck – Document Library & Download Manager
author: filedeck

sections.description:
FileDeck is a WordPress plugin for documents, downloads and client portals. It turns file collections into a fast, searchable document library with table, grid, gallery and folder layouts; tracks and protects every download; and gives each client a private document portal. List policies, guides, minutes, forms, resources, or any downloadable files — a PDF library, an Office-document archive, a mixed media collection — with instant search that filters as you type, and have a professional document library on your site in minutes. For teams that need more than a file list, Pro adds document management proper — version history, review and approval cycles, scheduled expiry and a full audit trail.

See it in action: try the live demo — the real plugin with a full sample library, no signup — or read the documentation.

A free version that’s actually usable. Every layout, every filter, and the Gutenberg block are free, and you can list as many documents as you like. Nothing essential is locked away just to force an upgrade.

What you won’t find elsewhere

  • Full-text document search – Pro searches inside your PDFs, Office and text files — text is extracted on your own server; only the optional OCR for scanned documents sends files off-site, and only when you switch it on
  • One-click migration – switching from Download Monitor, Simple Download Monitor, WordPress Download Manager, Document Library Lite/Pro, Shared Files, Simple File List, Advanced File Manager, BSK PDF Manager, Download Attachments, WP Customer Area or FileBird? FileDeck imports your whole library straight from your own database — no export files, no column mapping
  • Large file uploads – drawings, scans and video upload in resumable chunks, so your host’s upload limit is no longer the ceiling and a dropped connection resumes instead of restarting
  • Library event webhooks – a signed JSON POST when a document is published, updated, retired or deleted; point Zapier, Make or your own system at it
  • Client areas – give each client a private document portal with uploads and email notifications

Free features

  • Four layouts – searchable table, responsive card grid, a thumbnail-forward document gallery, or collapsible folders that follow your category hierarchy, sub-folders and all, in the order you choose
  • Instant search – filters as you type, no page reloads
  • Date-added filter – narrow a library to the past week, month or year (optional)
  • Year filter – a dropdown of the years the library’s documents span, read from their dates, for minutes, newsletters and reports filed by year (optional); year="2025" pins a library to one year
  • Reference number – a part number, document code or form number on every document: searchable, and a sortable column
  • Group by category – one library rendered as a titled section per category, with one search box across all of them, instead of a stacked library per category
  • AI-agent ready – read-only abilities for WordPress 6.9’s Abilities API, so agents can search the library through MCP
  • Sortable columns – title, date, size, type, downloads, and more
  • Unlimited documents – no cap; search scales automatically as your library grows
  • Download tracking – per-document download counts
  • Force download or open in browser – choose per document whether the button saves the file or displays it in the browser, instead of leaving it to each visitor’s browser defaults
  • Gutenberg block + shortcode + six page builders – native block with live preview, a [filedeck] shortcode, and native elements for Elementor (Library, Document Embed — also findable as “PDF Viewer” — and Search widgets), plus Library and Document Embed elements for Bricks, Divi, WPBakery (Visual Composer), Avada (Fusion Builder) and Beaver Builder — all with the same layout, filter and column options
  • Translation-ready, nine languages bundled – the library’s front end ships translated into Hungarian, Slovak, Spanish (Spain and Mexico), German, French (France and Canada), Italian, Polish, Brazilian Portuguese and Simplified Chinese, with a .pot template for translating it into any other language; documents and categories translate with WPML, Polylang and compatible plugins, and a bundled wpml-config.xml declares exactly how document data behaves (one file, many languages)
  • ⌘K command palette – site-wide quick-search overlay that jumps straight to any document
  • Sidebar widgets & Popular Documents block – Recent Documents and Top Downloads widgets for any sidebar, plus a Popular Documents block that puts the most-downloaded (or newest) list on any page; access-aware, so restricted documents never show to someone who cannot open them
  • QR codes – generate a printable QR for any document (offline, nothing leaves your site) for noticeboards and posters
  • Multi-select filters with counts – pick several categories or tags at once, see how many documents sit behind every option before you click, and drop any single one from the active-filter bar; put the filters above the library or under the column headings, and click a category in the table to filter by it
  • Multi-column sorting – click a heading to sort, shift-click a second to break the ties (file type, then newest first)
  • Shareable filtered views – search, filters, sort order and page all live in the URL with a one-click “copy link”; hover previews show a thumbnail and file details
  • Pagination your way – page numbers, a Load more button or infinite scroll, plus an optional fixed library height that scrolls the documents in place
  • External links – list documents hosted on Google Drive, Dropbox, SharePoint, or any URL — pasted Google Docs, Sheets, Slides and Drive links embed as live previews
  • Custom field & taxonomy columns – add any post meta (cf:field) or taxonomy (tax:slug) as a column; Pro adds the field builder that defines those fields, fields that apply only to chosen categories, and one-click import of your existing ACF field groups
  • Document previews – lightbox preview for PDFs and images, and featured images open in a lightbox from the image column
  • Inline document embed – embed a single document as an always-visible viewer on any page with the [filedeck_embed] shortcode, the Document Embed block or the Elementor widget: PDFs, images and Google links, with width and height controls, an optional download link and a full-screen button
  • Single document pages – a clean page with file details and a download button
  • Standalone search & links – [filedeck_search], [filedeck_login], and [filedeck_download] shortcodes
  • Styles to match any theme – a full design-token system: a “Match my theme” preset that inherits your theme’s colours, Minimal/Bordered/Compact presets, a built-in light/dark/auto colour scheme, accent + surface + text colours, plus link styles, custom download-button text, empty messages and pagination — no CSS required, and every element is a --fdk-* variable when you want to go further
  • Any file type – PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OpenDocument, images, audio, video, and more
  • Lightweight – no jQuery on the frontend; assets load only where a library appears
  • Theme template overrides – copy a template into your theme’s filedeck/ directory to replace library markup without forking the plugin; child theme first, then parent, then the plugin’s own copy
  • Accessible – keyboard-sortable columns, ARIA labels, screen-reader friendly

Switching from another plugin?

If you’re looking for a Download Monitor alternative, a WordPress Download Manager alternative, or a Document Library Pro alternative, FileDeck Pro imports your existing library in one click — documents, nested categories, tags, files, and (where the source records them) download counts and access rules — read straight from your own database. Shared Files libraries import the same way. No export files, no column mapping, safe to re-run, and we’ll help you move free if you’d like a hand.

Using Simple File List? Its wordpress.org listing has been closed since 23 July 2026 (the directory gives the reason as a security issue), so it can’t be installed or updated from the directory. If you’d rather move, FileDeck imports your entire Simple File List library in one click — files, folders and descriptions — straight from your own database.

FileDeck Pro

Upgrade for the features organizations need — from $59/year, your renewal never increases, and every purchase is covered by a 30-day money-back guarantee:

  • Full-text search inside files – search the text inside PDFs, Office documents and text files (optional OCR makes scanned PDFs searchable too); extraction runs on your own server, and results tell you which page of a PDF the match is on so you can jump straight to it
  • Access control – role restrictions on categories, password protection on a category or any single document, plus assigning a document to specific named people or to a group you define once and reuse — an assigned document is hidden from everyone else, not padlocked. Site-wide IP rules can limit downloads to your own networks, and a refused visitor can be sent to a page of your own instead of a dead end
  • Protected files – restricted files move to a deny-all vault and stream only after an access check, so direct file URLs stop working; optional signed links expire, for sharing with someone who can’t log in, and a single-use link works for exactly one download and then stops. Optional hotlink protection refuses downloads requested from other sites’ pages
  • Share button on every document – copy the link, open the device share sheet, or send it by email, X, Facebook, LinkedIn or WhatsApp; shares the document page, never the file, and loads nothing from any network until a visitor picks one
  • Client areas – per-client private portals with front-end submission, moderation and new-document emails; admit people by name, by group, by email domain so a whole company gets in without being listed one by one, or by membership plan (MemberPress, Paid Memberships Pro, WooCommerce Memberships, Restrict Content Pro, s2Member) — plan access follows the membership, so it goes when the membership lapses. Add a personal download history so each person can see what they already took, new/already-downloaded markers so a portal shows what has changed since their last visit, and favourites so a reader can keep their own shortlist
  • One-click migration – from Download Monitor, Simple Download Monitor, WordPress Download Manager, Document Library Lite/Pro, Shared Files, Simple File List, Advanced File Manager, BSK PDF Manager, Download Attachments, WP Customer Area and FileBird (see above)
  • Import a server folder – point FileDeck at a folder in your uploads directory and every file becomes a document, with sub-folders becoming nested categories; an optional daily re-scan imports new files on their own, so SFTP-ing a file in is enough to publish it
  • Automatic PDF thumbnails – plus Office, audio and video previews and inline embeds on top of the free PDF/image lightbox and embed
  • Self-hosted PDF viewer – embedded PDFs render from your own server with zoom, in-document find, print and full screen; because no external viewer service is involved, protected files, signed links and watermarked documents all display. Popup mode opens any embed in an overlay that loads only when clicked
  • Document lifecycle – version history, supersede with evergreen links, review cycles, approval workflow and auto-expiry, plus a public document changelog (a block or the [filedeck_changelog] shortcode) that lists published and updated documents newest first, grouped by month
  • Check-out & editing locks – claim a document while you prepare its next revision, so nobody else can replace the attached file until you check it back in
  • Downloads toolkit – email/webhook download notifications, daily quotas, per-document download limits (expire after N downloads), optional CAPTCHA bot friction (Cloudflare Turnstile or Google reCAPTCHA), lead capture with Mailchimp/Brevo sync, multi-select zip downloads with a select-all control in the table header, and Download all on a folder
  • Require a form before download – gate downloads behind Gravity Forms, Ninja Forms, WPForms, Contact Form 7 or any other form plugin you already use
  • Attach documents to a post – tick documents in the post editor and they list automatically at the end of the page
  • Terms before download – require readers to accept licence conditions or a disclaimer first, with every acceptance recorded in the activity log
  • Analytics & audit – activity log with per-document history (now including country, referrer and user agent), a running per-document view count you can show as a library column, analytics dashboard, optional GA4 events, CSV export
  • Search synonyms & spelling tolerance – teach the library your own shorthand so “PO” finds “purchase order”, and let a search that returned no results retry against the closest spelling in your titles and categories, saying which word it used
  • Search analytics – popular searches and a content-gap report of searches that found nothing, fed by every search box: library search, the command palette, full-text and AI search
  • Document feedback – anonymous “Was this helpful?” votes on document pages, with a least-helpful report (off until you enable it)
  • Cloud storage – browse and attach files from Amazon S3 or any S3-compatible service (Cloudflare R2, Wasabi, DigitalOcean Spaces), plus Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, SharePoint document libraries and Box
  • Vault offload – mirror protected files into an S3-compatible bucket and serve downloads by short-lived presigned link, so the bucket carries the bandwidth while every access check still runs first
  • Multisite shared libraries – render one site’s library on any other site of a WordPress network, with the source site’s access rules still enforcing
  • Publish & embed – put your whole library on any other website (Wix, Squarespace, Shopify, Webflow, Framer, or a custom front end) with one line of code; embeds show public documents only

Plus custom fields with faceted filtering, CSV import/export, bulk add from the Media Library, change subscriptions, a library health monitor, a GDPR toolkit and more — see every feature. An optional AI tier adds records governance — retention schedules, access certification, transmittals, acknowledgment tracking and PDF accessibility screening — plus semantic search, smart collections and “Ask this library”. Full pricing: https://www.getfiledeck.com/pricing/

Download Monitor, Simple Download Monitor, WordPress Download Manager, Document Library Pro, Document Library Lite, Shared Files, Simple File List, Advanced File Manager, BSK PDF Manager, Download Attachments, WP Customer Area, FileBird, and FileBird Document Library are trademarks of their respective owners; FileDeck is not affiliated with or endorsed by them.

Quick start

  1. Install and activate. FileDeck creates a “Document Library” page automatically.
  2. Go to Documents → Add New, add a title, and attach a file (or paste an external URL).
  3. Done — the document appears in your library instantly.

Use the Document Library block or the [filedeck] shortcode to place libraries anywhere:

[filedeck layout="grid" category="policies" columns="title,excerpt,size,link" per_page="20"]

Shortcode options

  • layout – table, grid, gallery, or folders
  • columns – comma-separated: id, image, title, excerpt, content, categories, tags, date, modified, author, size, type, filename, downloads, views, preview, link (views needs Pro activity logging)
  • category – limit to category slugs (comma-separated)
  • per_page – …
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin to wp-content/plugins/filedeck, or install it from Plugins → Add New in your WordPress admin.
  2. Activate the plugin. A Document Library page is created automatically.
  3. Go to Documents to add your files (from the Media Library or an external URL), and organize them with categories and tags.
  4. Add the Document Library block to any page or post — or use the [filedeck] shortcode — to display your library.
  5. Adjust layouts, columns, and styling under Documents → Settings.
sections.faq:
Is there a document limit?

No. The frontend automatically handles large libraries: small libraries get a zero-round-trip inline search index; larger ones paginate efficiently.

Can I link to files hosted elsewhere?

Yes — each document can use an uploaded file or an external URL (Google Drive, Dropbox, SharePoint, S3, YouTube, etc.).

Does it track downloads?

Yes, every document shows a running download count (visible in the admin list and optionally as a frontend column).

Does it work with my theme?

FileDeck uses minimal, namespaced styles designed to inherit your theme’s typography, and works with any properly-coded theme.

What do I get in the free version?

Every layout — table, grid, gallery and folders — plus instant search, sortable columns, multi-select filters with counts, the Gutenberg block, shortcodes, native Elementor, Bricks and Divi elements, download tracking, and no cap on how many documents you can list. Pro adds full-text search inside your files, access control, version history and one-click migration from other plugins.

Can visitors search inside my PDFs and Word documents?

With Pro, yes. Full-text search reads the contents of your PDFs, Office and text files — with optional OCR for scanned documents — and it runs on your own server, so your documents stay on your site.

Can I restrict documents to certain people?

With Pro, yes. Restrict a whole category or a single document by role, by password, to logged-in users, to named people, to a group you define once and reuse, or to everyone with an email address at a given domain. Restricted files move into a protected folder and are streamed through FileDeck rather than served from a guessable URL. Site-wide IP rules can additionally limit downloads to chosen networks.

Does it work with Elementor, Bricks or Divi?

Yes, and in the free version. FileDeck ships native Elementor widgets — Library, Document Embed (also listed as “PDF Viewer”) and Search — plus Library and Document Embed elements for Bricks and Divi, with the same layout, filter and column options as the block.

Can I move my library over from another plugin?

With Pro, yes — in one click, read straight from your own database, with no export files and no column mapping. Supported sources include Download Monitor, WordPress Download Manager, Document Library Lite and Pro, Shared Files, Simple Download Monitor, Simple File List, FileBird, BSK PDF Manager, Download Attachments, WP Customer Area and Advanced File Manager. The import is safe to re-run.

I’m on nginx — how do I protect restricted files?

FileDeck moves restricted documents’ files into wp-content/uploads/filedeck-protected/ and drops in an .htaccess deny rule. Apache honours that automatically. nginx ignores .htaccess, so add one location block to your server config and reload nginx:

location ^~ /wp-content/uploads/filedeck-protected/ { deny all; return 403; }

Until that rule is in place, authorised downloads still work (they are streamed through FileDeck), but the raw files in that folder remain directly reachable. On Apache (and most managed WordPress hosts), no action is needed.
sections.changelog:
2.101.1

  • Pro: signed-in visitors can download a restricted document whose file is a link to another site. The people it was shared with (logged-in users, named people, groups, membership plans, restricted categories, client areas) saw it in the library, but its Download button gave them an error instead of the file. The same fix covers the occasional restricted uploaded file that showed that error. Visitors without access still get no link. No setting needs changing: the fix takes effect the next time the page loads. On the AI plan, a view-only document whose file is a link to another site no longer shows a Download button.

2.101.0

  • The table layout keeps its shape while visitors search, filter, sort or page. Each column holds the width it had when the library first appeared, instead of re-flowing to fit whatever rows match. A table too wide for its space keeps its horizontal scroll, with its columns held too; phones, where rows stack as cards, are unchanged. To let columns resize as before, use stable_columns="0".
  • New stable_height="1" shortcode option: the library also keeps its first-page height, so a search with few or no matches doesn’t shrink it and move the rest of the page up.

2.100.1

  • Pro: a scanned PDF whose OCR attempt fails is now retried. If the OCR service timed out or was briefly unavailable, the document used to stay queued with no retry scheduled. Failed attempts now retry automatically with increasing gaps, a large scan has five minutes instead of two to finish, and the queue is spaced out so one background run isn’t handed the whole backlog at once.
  • Pro: the Search Index tab now shows how many scanned PDFs are queued for OCR, and when OCR has stopped on a document it says why (for example, the service didn’t answer in time or didn’t accept the key). Pressing Send tries those documents again.

2.100.0

  • Pro: scanned-PDF OCR is included with your license. Tick “Enable OCR” under Documents → Settings → Scanned OCR and it works; there is no OCR key to request or paste. Sites that already use a site key or their own OCR service keep working unchanged.

2.99.0

  • Translations now work alongside a wordpress.org language pack. A language pack for your language used to replace FileDeck’s bundled translations, and because a pack covers only the free plugin, Pro and AI tier text would have gone back to English. The pack now keeps priority for the strings it translates, and the bundled translations supply the rest.
  • The “Document Library” page FileDeck creates when it is first activated is titled in the site’s language when FileDeck has a translation for it.
  • AI tier: the PDF watermark footer is translated. It is printed in plain ASCII, so accented letters become plain ones where the server can transliterate them; otherwise, and for languages such as Chinese, the footer stays in English.
  • AI tier: the Smart Collections list shows when each collection was refreshed in the word order of your language (“vor 3 Stunden”, “il y a 3 heures”).
  • Security and reliability improvements.

2.98.1

  • The bundled translations now cover the “Document Category” and “Document Tag” names at the top of category and tag archive pages, the Documents menu’s own labels, and the Bricks document embed element’s settings and its prompt to pick a document.
  • Pro: the “This document has been superseded” notice, the “Attached documents” heading, the empty document changelog message and the placeholder choice at the top of dropdown document fields on the front-end submission form now use the bundled translations. They stayed in English on translated sites before.
  • AI tier: the read-and-confirm prompt with its button and confirmation messages, the “Related documents” heading and the empty collection message now use the bundled translations too.
  • Pro and AI tier: when the admin language is one of the nine, the Document Fields, Acknowledgments, Smart Collections and AI Index screens and the Supersede, Attached documents and Read & confirm boxes are translated as well. Other admin screens stay in English.

2.98.0

  • Fixed: on a fresh install the setup wizard opened before the opt-in question could appear, and while that question stayed unanswered the Documents menu held only the question and screens such as Upload Documents and Settings said “Sorry, you are not allowed to access this page.” The question now comes first, answering it (Allow or Skip) opens the setup wizard, and FileDeck works normally while it is still unanswered.
  • Uninstalling FileDeck moves the auto-created “Document Library” page to the trash when its title and content are still exactly as FileDeck created them, instead of leaving it published with a bare [filedeck] shortcode. It stays if it was edited, is the homepage, is in a menu or has child pages; on sites with the trash turned off it is set to draft.
  • The deactivation form’s “The plugin didn’t work”, “The plugin broke my site” and “The plugin suddenly stopped working” answers now offer an optional box for what happened, plus a link to tell us directly.
  • The setup wizard’s browser tab now reads “FileDeck Setup”.

2.97.0

  • The library’s “Copy link” button and its “Copied!” confirmation, “Load more”, the Previous, Next and page-number buttons, and the search palette’s label and messages now use the site’s translation. They stayed in English on translated sites before.
  • A translation template, languages/filedeck.pot, ships with the plugin, so Loco Translate, Poedit and similar tools list the plugin’s strings from the start instead of scanning its files (Loco skips large files by default, which left its list incomplete).
  • Canadian French (fr_CA) sites now get the bundled French translation.
  • FileDeck’s blocks now use a translation of their block editor labels when one is installed — a wordpress.org language pack or your own. The bundled translations cover the front end.
  • The bundled translations now also cover the year filter and the Reference column.
  • Pro: the preview window’s accessible name, the zip download’s error message, the embedded library’s frame title, the embed’s PDF loading message and the Bulk Add file picker are translatable too.

2.96.1

  • Fixed: on a phone, a document the visitor cannot open showed a padlock and a dash on its card with no label beside them to say what they were. They now carry their Download and Preview labels, laid out like the rest of the card.
  • Fixed: on a phone, a category name too long to sit beside its label ran off the edge of the document’s card. Categories that do not fit now move onto their own line, and a name longer than the whole card wraps inside its tag.

2.96.0

  • The deactivation form’s most common answer, “Expected something else”, now offers an optional box for what you were hoping FileDeck would do, plus a link to tell us directly. “Great, but I need a specific feature” asks which feature, and “Didn’t work as expected” asks what it did instead. All optional.

2.95.0

  • Year filter: an optional dropdown listing the years a library’s documents span, read from their dates — for minutes, newsletters and reports filed by year. show_year_filter="1" per library, or site-wide under Settings → Features; year="2025" pins a library to one year.
  • Reference number: a new field on every document for a part number, document code or form number. Searchable in the library and in content search, and available as a sortable “Reference” column. Included in the Pro CSV import and export.
  • Group by category: group_by="category" renders one library as a titled section per category (Folder order, then alphabetical; “Other” last) with one search box and one set of filters across all of them. Also on the Elementor widget and as a site-wide default.
  • Fixed: the date-added filter compared the displayed date against the cutoff in libraries with an inline index, so it could let old documents through. Both date filters now compare machine dates.
  • Fixed (Pro): a search the library matched by title, reference, category or tag was recorded as a content gap whenever the file text did not also match. The content-gaps report now records a gap only when nothing matched at all.

2.94.0

  • Sample documents now show only to logged-in editors (badged “Sample”); visitors, subscribers and embedded libraries do not see them — in any layout, on a document’s own page, or in the REST listing.
  • Trashing or deleting the last sample by hand now removes the empty sample categories, the same as the Remove button does.
  • The starter “Document Library” page unpublishes itself (it becomes a draft and is not deleted) once another published page renders a library — only if it is still exactly as activation wrote it. A notice says which page superseded it, with one-click restore.
  • Bundled translations of the library’s front end for Hungarian, Slovak, Spanish, German, French, Italian, Polish, Brazilian Portuguese and Simplified Chinese. A wordpress.org language pack still takes precedence.
  • An empty folders or grid library now says “No documents found” instead of rendering an empty frame.
  • The Document Categories screen notes how many categories hold no published documents, directly or in a sub-category.
  • The licence screen calls the paid build “Pro version”.
  • Sites five or more releases behind see a reminder on FileDeck’s own screens, with the release count and an update link.

2.93.0

  • Migrations now register a plugin-managed file that lives on your own site as a Media Library attachment where it already sits (not copied or moved), instead of linking it by URL. A URL-linked document had no zip checkbox, no preview button and no thumbnail; an attached one has all three. Applies to every importer (Pro).
  • Already migrated? Settings → Health now counts documents that link a local file by URL and attaches them in one click, 100 at a time — or all at once with wp filedeck attach-local-files.
  • The weekly health scan reports those documents as their own check rather than probing them as external links.

2.92.1

  • Hover preview cards are now off by default. Switch them on under Settings → Features → “Hover preview cards” if you want them.
  • Fixed: on sites where the card did show, it could render with no background — see-through, over the rows beneath it. It now carries its own surface, border and shadow.

2.92.0

  • New (Pro): a Share button on every document — in the library beside Download and on the document’s own page. It copies the link, opens the device’s share sheet where the browser has one, or sends the document by email, X, Facebook, LinkedIn or WhatsApp. Off by default: switch it on and pick the networks under Settings → Features, or per library with enable_share=”1″.
  • It shares the document page, never the file, so signed, gated and restricted downloads stay that way for whoever receives the link, and it loads nothing from any network until a visitor picks one.

2.89.0

  • Google reCAPTCHA v2 joins Cloudflare Turnstile as a bot-protection option (Pro). Pick the service under Settings → Submissions; the one choice covers both the download bot gate and the front-end submission form.
  • Switching service keeps the other service’s keys rather than deleting them, and a value that is neither reads as Turnstile rather than as no gate at all.

2.88.0

  • Theme template overrides: copy a template into your theme’s filedeck/ directory to replace library markup without forking the plugin. The table row and the empty state are overridable to start with; child theme wins, then parent, then the plugin’s own copy.
  • The files in the plugin’s templates/ directory are the ones FileDeck renders, so what you copy is exactly what you are replacing.

2.87.0

  • Native Document Library and Document Embed elements for WPBakery (Visual Composer), Avada (Fusion Builder) and Beaver Builder, joining the ones already there for Elementor, Bricks and Divi. Oxygen has no native element: use its Shortcode element with [filedeck].
  • The control-to-attribute map behind all of these now lives in one place, so a control cannot quietly stop working in one builder while it keeps working in the others.

2.86.0

  • Membership-plan gating (Pro): restrict a category or a document to holders of a MemberPress, Paid Memberships Pro, WooCommerce Memberships, Restrict Content Pro or s2Member plan. Access follows the membership, so when it lapses the document goes with it. Other membership plugins can register themselves with a filter.

2.85.0

  • Favourites (Pro): signed-in readers can star documents and read the list back on any page with [filedeck_my_favourites]. Access is re-checked when the list is read, so a document restricted since it was starred drops out of it.
  • A “New” marker now shows in the grid and gallery layouts too, not only in the table.

2.84.0

  • “Match my theme” now tries your theme’s second brand colour before falling back to your text colour. On themes whose first palette colour is a pale tint, the library used to turn black and white; it now picks up the colour your site actually uses.

2.83.0

  • New: AI agents can search your library. FileDeck registers three read-only abilities with WordPress 6.9’s Abilities API, so agents reach them through the MCP Adapter. Results are access-filtered — a restricted document does not appear, not even its title — and agents are given a page link rather than a download URL.

2.82.0

  • New: a “date added” filter — Any time / Past week / month / 3 months / year — so a long library narrows to what arrived recently. Off until you switch it on, and available per library. You can also pre-filter without showing the control with period="30".

2.81.0

  • New: a views column shows how many times each document has been looked at, sortable like any other column. Needs activity logging; with it off the column shows a dash rather than a zero.
  • New: Duplicate a document from the Documents list. The copy keeps categories, custom fields, access rules and delivery settings, starts as a draft, and does not inherit the original’s download or view counts.

2.80.0

  • The folders layout now follows your category hierarchy: a sub-category renders inside its parent, as deep as your categories go. Each folder’s count includes its sub-folders, and Download all on a parent takes them too.
  • New: a select-all checkbox in the table header ticks every document at once — or, in the folders layout, just that folder.

2.79.0

  • New: mark library rows as new since a signed-in visitor last looked, and dim the ones they have already downloaded. Read from the activity log and a per-person timestamp; logged-out visitors see no markers.
  • New: send someone who opens a document they cannot access to a page of your own — a “request access” page — instead of a not-found page. Documents assigned to named people, to a group, or filed in a client area keep the not-found page, so their existence is not disclosed.

2.78.0

  • New: search synonyms. Define groups of equivalent terms so “PO” finds “purchase order”. Each word you type is still required; a synonym only widens what satisfies it.
  • New: spelling tolerance. A search that returned no results is retried against the closest spelling from your titles, categories and tags, and the library says which word it used. Only ever a fallback — a search that found something is not second-guessed.

2.77.0

  • New: groups. Name a set of people once, then give that group a client area or an individual document. Change the membership and every grant follows.
  • Fixed: a document shared with a group now appears in that member’s library, not only on its own page.

2.76.0

  • New: admit a whole company to a client area by email domain, so someone who joins that domain later gets in without the category being edited. Named people, groups and domains are all honoured together.
  • New: [filedeck_my_downloads] shows a signed-in visitor what they have already downloaded. Documents they can no longer access drop out of the list.

2.75.0

  • New: single-use download links. A link that works for exactly one download and then stops, for sending a document to one person. It expires after 7 days if unused.
  • New: optional hotlink protection refuses downloads requested from another site’s pages. Requests with no referrer, and signed share links, are unaffected.

2.74.0

  • New: IP rules. Limit downloads to chosen addresses or CIDR ranges, or block specific ones. Applies to every download, signed share links included. Site administrators keep access, so a mistyped rule cannot lock you out.
  • New: assigning a document to named people now emails them, the same as publishing into a client area already did.

2.73.1

  • “Match my theme” now inherits from far more themes. It already read block-theme palettes; it now also reads Astra, Kadence, GeneratePress, OceanWP, Blocksy, Neve, Lightning, Sydney and Elementor’s global colours.

  • Fixed: on Twenty Twenty-Five, “Match my theme” did not pick up the theme’s accent colours and used the FileDeck blue instead.

2.72.7

  • Fixed: an uninstall helper used a direct PHP file check where WordPress’s own wrapper is required. No behaviour change; it clears a wordpress.org review error.

2.72.6

  • Fixed: labels that share the filter-chip style — the “AI tier” tag beside a setting, for example — were drawn with a “×” as though you could dismiss them. The × now appears only on an active filter chip, which is the one you can actually remove.

2.72.5

  • Fixed: the “enter your details to download” form and the document preview box are now announced properly by screen readers — both fields have real labels and autofill hints, and each box identifies itself as a dialog.
  • Changed: this readme’s feature list now covers check-out & editing locks, server-folder import, vault offload and multisite shared libraries, all of which already shipped, and describes access control accurately (role restrictions apply to categories; password protection applies to either).

2.72.4

  • Fixed (AI tier): a document whose title contains an ampersand was listed under an “Ask this library” answer with the raw HTML code showing — “Returns & Refunds Policy” instead of “Returns & Refunds Policy”. The title is also now passed to the AI unescaped.

2.72.3

  • Fixed (AI tier): answers from Fireworks models could contain stray citation markers such as 【1†L1-L4】 in the middle of a sentence. They are now rendered as [1], matching the numbered sources listed under the answer.
  • Changed (AI tier): Fireworks requests now ask for a low reasoning budget. Reasoning counts against the answer’s token allowance, so this makes answers cheaper and faster, and stops a long deliberation from using up the whole budget and returning nothing. Models that don’t accept the setting are detected and retried without it.

2.72.2

  • Added (AI tier): Fireworks AI joins Anthropic and OpenAI as a chat provider for “Ask this library” and the AI summary & tag suggestions. Bring your own Fireworks key; the default model is gpt-oss-120b, and you can set any Fireworks model id (a bare id is qualified for you).
  • Changed: the chat provider list on the Settings screen is now built from the registered providers, so a provider added by the filedeck_chat_providers filter is both selectable and saveable.
  • Fixed: this readme described the AI features as part of Pro. They are the separate AI tier and are not included in Pro.

2.72.1

  • Fixed: if a second copy of FileDeck was installed alongside the first (most often the Pro download added as its own folder while the free version was still active), activating it failed with WordPress’s “plugin could not be activated because it triggered a fatal error”. FileDeck now stands down cleanly and tells you which copy is running and which to remove.
  • Added: document revision history. Edits to a document’s description are recoverable from the editor, the same as posts and pages.
  • Fixed: “Custom order” under Documents > Settings > Library now works. The option was selectable but there was no way to set an order, so it had no effect; documents now have an Order field in the editor sidebar.

2.72.0

  • Security and reliability improvements across document access, imports and outbound email.
  • Changed (Pro): per-role daily download allowances apply to signed-in visitors, counted per person. If you have per-role allowances configured, check the numbers under Documents > Settings > Downloads after updating — some may not have been taking effect.
  • Changed (Pro): documents with a download limit, and sites with download allowances configured, are no longer served to automated clients such as search engines, link previews and uptime monitors. A bot can no longer spend a limited document’s allowance, and people are unaffected.
  • Changed (Pro): the activity log records the signed-in person against downloads, terms acceptances and acknowledgements, and files acknowledgements, transmittals, retention and access reviews under their own event types rather than counting them as downloads. Existing reports will change shape accordingly.
  • Changed (Pro): importing from another document plugin no longer publishes items the source was keeping out of public view — where the source stores documents as posts, anything draft, pending or private arrives as a FileDeck draft for you to review and publish.
  • Changed (AI): a watermarked PDF carries the downloader’s email address when they are signed in, as intended, rather than always reading “a visitor”.
  • Changed (Pro): uninstalling leaves a plain-text note in the protected-files folder explaining what is in there and how to get it back. The files stay protected — removing the plugin does not make restricted documents publicly downloadable.
  • Fixed (Pro): “Delete all data on uninstall” also removes transmittal records and smart collections. Uninstalling now clears FileDeck’s scheduled tasks either way.
  • Fixed (Pro): a category password containing symbols such as % or < is stored exactly as typed. If you set one that never accepted the password you chose, re-save it.
  • Fixed (AI): starting a PDF accessibility scan completes in the background and fills in the report.

2.71.2

  • Fixed: on a short browser window, a filter with a long list of categories now shrinks and scrolls rather than running off the top or bottom of the screen.

2.71.1

  • Fixed: opening a category, tag or custom-field filter pushed the whole document table down the page. The filter panel now opens over the library instead of inside it, so nothing moves, and it closes when you click away or press Escape.

2.71.0

  • Added: the free version now says what the paid tiers add, at the point it is relevant — a preview of the Visibility control on the document screen, the Settings sections Pro adds, a note when another document plugin on the same site has documents FileDeck could import, and a note about searching inside files once a library grows past a few hundred documents. Each one is dismissible for good, none of them block anything, and nothing that worked before has been locked or removed.

2.70.1

  • Fixed (Pro): the new bulk access actions changed a document’s visibility without moving its file into the protected vault, so documents bulk-restricted in 2.70.0 were hidden from libraries while their files stayed publicly reachable. Re-apply the access change on any documents you bulk-restricted, or re-save them, and the files will be protected correctly.
  • Fixed (Pro): a document assigned to specific people is now visible to administrators in libraries, as described. It was being hidden from them too.
  • Fixed (Pro): the list of people on a document now always includes everyone already assigned, however many users the site has. Previously, on sites with more than 200 users, re-saving a document could drop an assignee who was not shown.
  • Fixed (Pro): the people picker is only shown to users who are allowed to list site users, and email addresses are hidden from anyone who is not.
  • Fixed (Pro): deleting a user, or removing them from a site, now clears their document assignments.
  • Fixed (Pro): “Download all” on a folder now downloads the documents you can see, rather than the whole folder, when a search or filter is narrowing it.

2.70.0

  • Added (Pro): assign a document to specific people. Only they (and administrators) can see or download it — and it does not appear in anyone else’s library at all, not even as a locked row, so one client can never learn what another client has.
  • Added (Pro): “Download all” on a folder, which zips everything in it in one go. It passes the same lead-capture, terms and bot checks as any other download.
  • Added (Pro): bulk access changes from the Documents list — make a selection public or logged-in-only in one action, for reorganising a large import.

2.69.0

  • Fixed: a library added to the page after it loads — by a page builder’s tabs or popup, a theme’s own scripting, or anything else that inserts content later — now starts properly instead of rendering correctly and then doing nothing. Previously its search box, filters and sortable columns were all inert, with nothing to indicate why.
  • Added (developers): window.filedeckInit( element ) starts any library that isn’t already running, and each one fires a bubbling fdk:ready event as it starts. Safe to call more than once — a library that is already running is left alone.

A section appears once you have at least two of its screens, so a screen you have on its own simply keeps its own entry.

  • Fixed: the empty-state message swap no longer rewrites the whole element, so the link survives search/filter changes.

short_description: Document libraries, tracked downloads and client portals — every layout free (table, grid, gallery, folders), instant search, no document limit.
description:
FileDeck is a WordPress plugin for documents, downloads and client portals. It turns file collections into a fast, searchable document library with table, grid, gallery and folder layouts; tracks and protects every download; and gives each client a private document portal. List policies, guides, minutes, forms, resources, or any downloadable files — a PDF library, an Office-document archive, a mixed media collection — with instant search that filters as you type, and have a professional document library on your site in minutes. For teams that need more than a file list, Pro adds document management proper — version history, review and approval cycles, scheduled expiry and a full audit trail.

See it in action: try the live demo — the real plugin with a full sample library, no signup — or read the documentation.

A free version that’s actually usable. Every layout, every filter, and the Gutenberg block are free, and you can list as many documents as you like. Nothing essential is locked away just to force an upgrade.

What you won’t find elsewhere

  • Full-text document search – Pro searches inside your PDFs, Office and text files — text is extracted on your own server; only the optional OCR for scanned documents sends files off-site, and only when you switch it on
  • One-click migration – switching from Download Monitor, Simple Download Monitor, WordPress Download Manager, Document Library Lite/Pro, Shared Files, Simple File List, Advanced File Manager, BSK PDF Manager, Download Attachments, WP Customer Area or FileBird? FileDeck imports your whole library straight from your own database — no export files, no column mapping
  • Large file uploads – drawings, scans and video upload in resumable chunks, so your host’s upload limit is no longer the ceiling and a dropped connection resumes instead of restarting
  • Library event webhooks – a signed JSON POST when a document is published, updated, retired or deleted; point Zapier, Make or your own system at it
  • Client areas – give each client a private document portal with uploads and email notifications

Free features

  • Four layouts – searchable table, responsive card grid, a thumbnail-forward document gallery, or collapsible folders that follow your category hierarchy, sub-folders and all, in the order you choose
  • Instant search – filters as you type, no page reloads
  • Date-added filter – narrow a library to the past week, month or year (optional)
  • Year filter – a dropdown of the years the library’s documents span, read from their dates, for minutes, newsletters and reports filed by year (optional); year="2025" pins a library to one year
  • Reference number – a part number, document code or form number on every document: searchable, and a sortable column
  • Group by category – one library rendered as a titled section per category, with one search box across all of them, instead of a stacked library per category
  • AI-agent ready – read-only abilities for WordPress 6.9’s Abilities API, so agents can search the library through MCP
  • Sortable columns – title, date, size, type, downloads, and more
  • Unlimited documents – no cap; search scales automatically as your library grows
  • Download tracking – per-document download counts
  • Force download or open in browser – choose per document whether the button saves the file or displays it in the browser, instead of leaving it to each visitor’s browser defaults
  • Gutenberg block + shortcode + six page builders – native block with live preview, a [filedeck] shortcode, and native elements for Elementor (Library, Document Embed — also findable as “PDF Viewer” — and Search widgets), plus Library and Document Embed elements for Bricks, Divi, WPBakery (Visual Composer), Avada (Fusion Builder) and Beaver Builder — all with the same layout, filter and column options
  • Translation-ready, nine languages bundled – the library’s front end ships translated into Hungarian, Slovak, Spanish (Spain and Mexico), German, French (France and Canada), Italian, Polish, Brazilian Portuguese and Simplified Chinese, with a .pot template for translating it into any other language; documents and categories translate with WPML, Polylang and compatible plugins, and a bundled wpml-config.xml declares exactly how document data behaves (one file, many languages)
  • ⌘K command palette – site-wide quick-search overlay that jumps straight to any document
  • Sidebar widgets & Popular Documents block – Recent Documents and Top Downloads widgets for any sidebar, plus a Popular Documents block that puts the most-downloaded (or newest) list on any page; access-aware, so restricted documents never show to someone who cannot open them
  • QR codes – generate a printable QR for any document (offline, nothing leaves your site) for noticeboards and posters
  • Multi-select filters with counts – pick several categories or tags at once, see how many documents sit behind every option before you click, and drop any single one from the active-filter bar; put the filters above the library or under the column headings, and click a category in the table to filter by it
  • Multi-column sorting – click a heading to sort, shift-click a second to break the ties (file type, then newest first)
  • Shareable filtered views – search, filters, sort order and page all live in the URL with a one-click “copy link”; hover previews show a thumbnail and file details
  • Pagination your way – page numbers, a Load more button or infinite scroll, plus an optional fixed library height that scrolls the documents in place
  • External links – list documents hosted on Google Drive, Dropbox, SharePoint, or any URL — pasted Google Docs, Sheets, Slides and Drive links embed as live previews
  • Custom field & taxonomy columns – add any post meta (cf:field) or taxonomy (tax:slug) as a column; Pro adds the field builder that defines those fields, fields that apply only to chosen categories, and one-click import of your existing ACF field groups
  • Document previews – lightbox preview for PDFs and images, and featured images open in a lightbox from the image column
  • Inline document embed – embed a single document as an always-visible viewer on any page with the [filedeck_embed] shortcode, the Document Embed block or the Elementor widget: PDFs, images and Google links, with width and height controls, an optional download link and a full-screen button
  • Single document pages – a clean page with file details and a download button
  • Standalone search & links – [filedeck_search], [filedeck_login], and [filedeck_download] shortcodes
  • Styles to match any theme – a full design-token system: a “Match my theme” preset that inherits your theme’s colours, Minimal/Bordered/Compact presets, a built-in light/dark/auto colour scheme, accent + surface + text colours, plus link styles, custom download-button text, empty messages and pagination — no CSS required, and every element is a --fdk-* variable when you want to go further
  • Any file type – PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OpenDocument, images, audio, video, and more
  • Lightweight – no jQuery on the frontend; assets load only where a library appears
  • Theme template overrides – copy a template into your theme’s filedeck/ directory to replace library markup without forking the plugin; child theme first, then parent, then the plugin’s own copy
  • Accessible – keyboard-sortable columns, ARIA labels, screen-reader friendly

Switching from another plugin?

If you’re looking for a Download Monitor alternative, a WordPress Download Manager alternative, or a Document Library Pro alternative, FileDeck Pro imports your existing library in one click — documents, nested categories, tags, files, and (where the source records them) download counts and access rules — read straight from your own database. Shared Files libraries import the same way. No export files, no column mapping, safe to re-run, and we’ll help you move free if you’d like a hand.

Using Simple File List? Its wordpress.org listing has been closed since 23 July 2026 (the directory gives the reason as a security issue), so it can’t be installed or updated from the directory. If you’d rather move, FileDeck imports your entire Simple File List library in one click — files, folders and descriptions — straight from your own database.

FileDeck Pro

Upgrade for the features organizations need — from $59/year, your renewal never increases, and every purchase is covered by a 30-day money-back guarantee:

  • Full-text search inside files – search the text inside PDFs, Office documents and text files (optional OCR makes scanned PDFs searchable too); extraction runs on your own server, and results tell you which page of a PDF the match is on so you can jump straight to it
  • Access control – role restrictions on categories, password protection on a category or any single document, plus assigning a document to specific named people or to a group you define once and reuse — an assigned document is hidden from everyone else, not padlocked. Site-wide IP rules can limit downloads to your own networks, and a refused visitor can be sent to a page of your own instead of a dead end
  • Protected files – restricted files move to a deny-all vault and stream only after an access check, so direct file URLs stop working; optional signed links expire, for sharing with someone who can’t log in, and a single-use link works for exactly one download and then stops. Optional hotlink protection refuses downloads requested from other sites’ pages
  • Share button on every document – copy the link, open the device share sheet, or send it by email, X, Facebook, LinkedIn or WhatsApp; shares the document page, never the file, and loads nothing from any network until a visitor picks one
  • Client areas – per-client private portals with front-end submission, moderation and new-document emails; admit people by name, by group, by email domain so a whole company gets in without being listed one by one, or by membership plan (MemberPress, Paid Memberships Pro, WooCommerce Memberships, Restrict Content Pro, s2Member) — plan access follows the membership, so it goes when the membership lapses. Add a personal download history so each person can see what they already took, new/already-downloaded markers so a portal shows what has changed since their last visit, and favourites so a reader can keep their own shortlist
  • One-click migration – from Download Monitor, Simple Download Monitor, WordPress Download Manager, Document Library Lite/Pro, Shared Files, Simple File List, Advanced File Manager, BSK PDF Manager, Download Attachments, WP Customer Area and FileBird (see above)
  • Import a server folder – point FileDeck at a folder in your uploads directory and every file becomes a document, with sub-folders becoming nested categories; an optional daily re-scan imports new files on their own, so SFTP-ing a file in is enough to publish it
  • Automatic PDF thumbnails – plus Office, audio and video previews and inline embeds on top of the free PDF/image lightbox and embed
  • Self-hosted PDF viewer – embedded PDFs render from your own server with zoom, in-document find, print and full screen; because no external viewer service is involved, protected files, signed links and watermarked documents all display. Popup mode opens any embed in an overlay that loads only when clicked
  • Document lifecycle – version history, supersede with evergreen links, review cycles, approval workflow and auto-expiry, plus a public document changelog (a block or the [filedeck_changelog] shortcode) that lists published and updated documents newest first, grouped by month
  • Check-out & editing locks – claim a document while you prepare its next revision, so nobody else can replace the attached file until you check it back in
  • Downloads toolkit – email/webhook download notifications, daily quotas, per-document download limits (expire after N downloads), optional CAPTCHA bot friction (Cloudflare Turnstile or Google reCAPTCHA), lead capture with Mailchimp/Brevo sync, multi-select zip downloads with a select-all control in the table header, and Download all on a folder
  • Require a form before download – gate downloads behind Gravity Forms, Ninja Forms, WPForms, Contact Form 7 or any other form plugin you already use
  • Attach documents to a post – tick documents in the post editor and they list automatically at the end of the page
  • Terms before download – require readers to accept licence conditions or a disclaimer first, with every acceptance recorded in the activity log
  • Analytics & audit – activity log with per-document history (now including country, referrer and user agent), a running per-document view count you can show as a library column, analytics dashboard, optional GA4 events, CSV export
  • Search synonyms & spelling tolerance – teach the library your own shorthand so “PO” finds “purchase order”, and let a search that returned no results retry against the closest spelling in your titles and categories, saying which word it used
  • Search analytics – popular searches and a content-gap report of searches that found nothing, fed by every search box: library search, the command palette, full-text and AI search
  • Document feedback – anonymous “Was this helpful?” votes on document pages, with a least-helpful report (off until you enable it)
  • Cloud storage – browse and attach files from Amazon S3 or any S3-compatible service (Cloudflare R2, Wasabi, DigitalOcean Spaces), plus Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, SharePoint document libraries and Box
  • Vault offload – mirror protected files into an S3-compatible bucket and serve downloads by short-lived presigned link, so the bucket carries the bandwidth while every access check still runs first
  • Multisite shared libraries – render one site’s library on any other site of a WordPress network, with the source site’s access rules still enforcing
  • Publish & embed – put your whole library on any other website (Wix, Squarespace, Shopify, Webflow, Framer, or a custom front end) with one line of code; embeds show public documents only

Plus custom fields with faceted filtering, CSV import/export, bulk add from the Media Library, change subscriptions, a library health monitor, a GDPR toolkit and more — see every feature. An optional AI tier adds records governance — retention schedules, access certification, transmittals, acknowledgment tracking and PDF accessibility screening — plus semantic search, smart collections and “Ask this library”. Full pricing: https://www.getfiledeck.com/pricing/

Download Monitor, Simple Download Monitor, WordPress Download Manager, Document Library Pro, Document Library Lite, Shared Files, Simple File List, Advanced File Manager, BSK PDF Manager, Download Attachments, WP Customer Area, FileBird, and FileBird Document Library are trademarks of their respective owners; FileDeck is not affiliated with or endorsed by them.

Quick start

  1. Install and activate. FileDeck creates a “Document Library” page automatically.
  2. Go to Documents → Add New, add a title, and attach a file (or paste an external URL).
  3. Done — the document appears in your library instantly.

Use the Document Library block or the [filedeck] shortcode to place libraries anywhere:

[filedeck layout="grid" category="policies" columns="title,excerpt,size,link" per_page="20"]

Shortcode options

  • layout – table, grid, gallery, or folders
  • columns – comma-separated: id, image, title, excerpt, content, categories, tags, date, modified, author, size, type, filename, downloads, views, preview, link (views needs Pro activity logging)
  • category – limit to category slugs (comma-separated)
  • per_page – …
